summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, tracheostomy, and a history of recurrent infections was admitted with altered mental status and respiratory failure. He was found to have multifocal pneumonia due to Serratia and Proteus, requiring intubation and ventilator support, and a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus urinary tract infection. He was treated with cefepime for pneumonia and linezolid for the UTI, with successful weaning from the ventilator. His altered mental status, attributed to toxic metabolic encephalopathy, resolved with treatment. The citalopram dose was temporarily reduced due to interaction risk with linezolid. He was discharged to extended care on day 7 to complete his antibiotic courses, with glycopyrrolate added to manage secretions.
problems: Pneumonia due to other Gram-negative bacteria
Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
